overall: The AG found the task force is a public body subject to the Open Meeting Law and violated it by members failing to certify receipt of OML materials within two weeks; the AG declined the Section 22 and formation-vote allegations and ordered certification, minutes, and future compliance.

allegations.summary: Members of the task force allegedly did not certify receipt of Open Meeting Law materials within two weeks of qualifying for office.
allegations.key_passage: Because Task Force members did not certify receipt of the Open Meeting Law materials within two weeks of qualification for office, we find that the Task Force violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged non-compliance with 'relevant parts of Section 22' regarding 'documents and other exhibits,' without specifics.
allegations.key_passage: Because the complainant does not direct us to the specifics of the alleged non-compliance, we decline to review this allegation.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the task force's formation should have been the subject of a School Committee vote.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review the allegation that a vote was not taken to create the Task Force because even if there were no vote (and it appears that there was none), this would not constitute a violation of the Open Meeting Law.

remedy: Within 14 days, task force members certify receipt of Open Meeting Law materials and provide the certification to the Falmouth town clerk.
Within 60 days, the task force creates minutes of its meetings held to date and certifies to the AG's office that it has done so.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.
remedy_passage: We order that within 14 days of the date of this letter, members of the Task Force certify receipt of Open Meeting Law materials and provide such certification to the Falmouth town clerk.
